title: One event an operation reports before its response
description: Events exist so a caller can display progress while work is running. They are never the authoritative answer: the response carries every diagnostic an event carried, so a consumer that ignores events loses responsiveness and nothing else. Adding an event kind is additive; a consumer must tolerate one it does not know by ignoring it.

event.description: Which kind of event this is. A consumer dispatches on this and never on which fields happen to be present.

oneOf.title: started
oneOf.description: Work has begun. Exactly one per operation that reports events, always first.

oneOf.title: progress
oneOf.description: How far one named phase has got. Phases arrive in the order the handler reaches them.

phase.description: A stable identifier for the phase. Not a human message; it may be used as a map key.

total.description: Absent when the handler does not yet know the total, which a consumer must render as indeterminate rather than as zero.

oneOf.title: diagnostic
oneOf.description: A finding reported early. The same diagnostic also appears on the response.

oneOf.title: truncated
oneOf.description: The event budget was exhausted. Always last if present, and emitted once, so a truncated stream is never mistaken for a complete one.

emitted.description: How many events were delivered before the budget ran out.
